chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ubaydillah ibn Mu'awiya ibn Shurayh, from his father, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a man comes while the Imam is bowing (ruku'), a single takbirah suffices for his entry into the prayer and the bowing.'

And whenever a person misses a rakah or more than that with the Imam, he should pray with him what remains, and that should be considered his first entry into the prayer, and he should pray it according to the measure he would pray if he had started the prayer from the beginning. The elaboration of this statement is what he narrated:

key_terms.فَاتَ الْإِنْسَانَ رَكْعَةٌ: A rakah was missed by the person
key_terms.لِدُخُولِهِ فِي الصَّلَاةِ: For his entry into the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for joining congregational prayer when the Imam is already bowing?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of 'joining' (muqararah) rather than 'catching' (adراك) when entering late, ensuring the missed rakah is treated as the first unit of the worshipper's prayer. It clarifies that the single takbir serves a dual function for both entry and the bowing posture, streamlining the transition for the latecomer. This reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of congregational unity while maintaining the structural integrity of the individual prayer count.
